---
title: "About — Sleep & Physical Strength"
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(survey)
library(scales)

df <- read_rds("data/processed/nhanes_sleep_strength.rds")
sample_flow <- read_csv("data/processed/sample_flow.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

demo_mec <- bind_rows(
  read_xpt("data/raw/DEMO_G.XPT") |> mutate(cycle = "2011-2012") |> select(SEQN, cycle, SDMVPSU, SDMVSTRA, WTMEC2YR),
  read_xpt("data/raw/DEMO_H.XPT") |> mutate(cycle = "2013-2014") |> select(SEQN, cycle, SDMVPSU, SDMVSTRA, WTMEC2YR)
) |>
  filter(WTMEC2YR > 0) |>
  mutate(mec_weight_4yr = WTMEC2YR / 2) |>
  left_join(df |> select(-cycle, -mec_weight_4yr) |> mutate(in_cohort = TRUE), by = "SEQN") |>
  mutate(in_cohort = coalesce(in_cohort, FALSE))

des_mec_full <- svydesign(
  id = ~SDMVPSU, strata = ~SDMVSTRA, weights = ~mec_weight_4yr,
  nest = TRUE, data = demo_mec
)
des_analytic <- subset(des_mec_full, in_cohort)

n_total <- nrow(df)
n_male <- sum(df$sex == "Male")
n_female <- sum(df$sex == "Female")
n_top80 <- sum(df$age == 80)
n_75plus <- sum(df$age_group == "75-80+")
n_mec_universe <- nrow(demo_mec)
n_strata <- n_distinct(demo_mec$SDMVSTRA)
n_psu <- n_distinct(paste(demo_mec$SDMVSTRA, demo_mec$SDMVPSU))
n_degf <- as.integer(degf(des_analytic))

# Programmatic missingness table across analytical dataset variables
missing_summary <- tibble(
  variable = c(
    "Core Analytical Variables (SEQN, age, sex, sleep_hours, combined_grip_kg, max_hand_grip_kg, race_ethnicity, mec_weight_4yr)",
    "trouble_sleeping (SLQ050 — Told doctor trouble sleeping)",
    "sleep_disorder (SLQ060 — Told by doctor have sleep disorder)",
    "income_pir (INDFMPIR — Family income-to-poverty ratio)"
  ),
  complete_n = c(
    n_total,
    sum(!is.na(df$trouble_sleeping)),
    sum(!is.na(df$sleep_disorder)),
    sum(!is.na(df$income_pir))
  ),
  missing_n = c(
    0L,
    sum(is.na(df$trouble_sleeping)),
    sum(is.na(df$sleep_disorder)),
    sum(is.na(df$income_pir))
  ),
  handling = c(
    "Required for cohort inclusion (100% complete across N = 10,987)",
    "NHANES codes 7/9 recoded to NA; excluded via domain subset() when analyzing SLQ050",
    "NHANES codes 7/9 recoded to NA; excluded via domain subset() when analyzing SLQ060",
    "Unreported household income retained as NA in master file; complete-case domain subset (n = 10,119) used for PIR analyses"
  )
) |>
  mutate(missing_pct = sprintf("%.2f%%", (missing_n / n_total) * 100))
```

<section class="glass-card" style="margin-bottom: 0;">
<div class="section-kicker">Research Arc &amp; Observational Scope</div>
<h2 class="section-title" style="margin-bottom: 0.65rem;">Project Motivation &amp; Limitations</h2>
<div class="prose-block">
<p>
This project began with a question rooted in athletic performance and recovery—whether habitual short sleep aligns with lower physical force—and broadened into an examination of upper-body strength across biological sex and the human lifespan (`ages 16–80+`).
</p>
<p style="font-size: 0.92rem; color: #94a3b8;">
<strong>Key study limitations:</strong> NHANES is a cross-sectional observational survey, so associations cannot establish causality or rule out reverse causation (such as underlying illness increasing sleep duration in older age). Sleep duration (`SLD010H`) is self-reported in whole hours rather than actigraphy-measured, and unmerged NHANES modules—such as body anthropometric measures (`BMX`) and physical activity (`PAQ`)—are outside the three-module scope of this repository.
</p>
</div>
</section>
</div>

<!-- DATA SOURCES -->
<section class="glass-card">
<div class="section-kicker">Data Provenance</div>
<h2 class="section-title" style="margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">CDC/NCHS NHANES 2011–2014 Public-Use Data Sources</h2>
<div class="prose-block">
<p>
All analyses use public-use SAS transport (`.XPT`) files published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) across two consecutive two-year waves: <strong>2011–2012 (Cycle G)</strong> and <strong>2013–2014 (Cycle H)</strong>. These two waves constitute the dedicated NHANES cycles in which objective bilateral handgrip dynamometry was administered in the Mobile Examination Center (MEC). Raw files are stored unmodified in <code>data/raw/</code> and merged deterministically by respondent sequence number (<code>SEQN</code>) in <code>scripts/prepare_data.R</code>:
</p>
</div>

<div class="info-grid-3">
<div class="mini-panel">
<span class="code-tag">DEMO_G.XPT &amp; DEMO_H.XPT</span>
<h4>Demographics &amp; Survey Design</h4>
<p style="font-size: 0.88rem; color: #cbd5e1; margin: 0;">
Provides examinee age (`RIDAGEYR`, top-coded at `80`), biological sex (`RIAGENDR`), race/Hispanic origin (`RIDRETH3`), family income-to-poverty ratio (`INDFMPIR`), 2-year MEC exam weights (`WTMEC2YR`), masked variance pseudo-strata (`SDMVSTRA`), and pseudo-PSUs (`SDMVPSU`).
</p>
</div>

<div class="mini-panel">
<span class="code-tag">SLQ_G.XPT &amp; SLQ_H.XPT</span>
<h4>Sleep Disorders Questionnaire</h4>
<p style="font-size: 0.88rem; color: #cbd5e1; margin: 0;">
Administered during the household interview to participants aged `16` and older. Captures usual weekday/workday sleep hours (`SLD010H`), whether the participant ever told a doctor they had trouble sleeping (`SLQ050`), and physician-diagnosed sleep disorders (`SLQ060`).
</p>
</div>

<div class="mini-panel">
<span class="code-tag">MGX_G.XPT &amp; MGX_H.XPT</span>
<h4>Muscle Strength — Grip Test</h4>
<p style="font-size: 0.88rem; color: #cbd5e1; margin: 0;">
Objective isometric upper-body strength measured in the MEC using a Takei Digital Grip Strength Dynamometer across three trials per hand (`MGXH1T1–MGXH2T3`), yielding CDC's combined grip metric (`MGDCGSZ`, sum of the best reading from each hand).
</p>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- VARIABLE DICTIONARY -->
<section class="glass-card">
<div class="section-kicker">Codebook</div>
<h2 class="section-title" style="margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Analytical Variable Dictionary</h2>
<p class="section-desc" style="margin-bottom: 0.85rem;">
Definitions, units, and recoding rules for variables in <code>data/processed/nhanes_sleep_strength.rds</code> (`N = `r comma(n_total)` examinees) and joined survey-design identifiers.
</p>

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">
<table class="dark-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Analytical Variable</th>
<th>NHANES Source</th>
<th>Measurement &amp; Coding</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>SEQN</code>, <code>cycle</code></td>
<td><code>DEMO_G/H</code></td>
<td>Unique respondent identifier merged across modules; survey wave indicator (`2011-2012` vs. `2013-2014`).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>age</code>, <code>age_group</code></td>
<td><code>RIDAGEYR</code></td>
<td>Age in years at screening (`16` to `80`; `n = `r comma(n_top80)`` examinees aged `80+` in our final cohort are top-coded at `80` by NCHS). Grouped into `16-29`, `30-44`, `45-59`, `60-74`, and `75-80+` (`n = `r comma(n_75plus)`` total in `75-80+`).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sex</code></td>
<td><code>RIAGENDR</code></td>
<td>Biological sex coded `1 = Male` (`n = `r comma(n_male)``), `2 = Female` (`n = `r comma(n_female)``).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sleep_hours</code>, <code>sleep_category</code></td>
<td><code>SLD010H</code></td>
<td>Self-reported usual weekday/workday sleep duration in whole hours (`2` to `12+`; special codes `77` Refused and `99` Don't Know recoded to `NA`). Grouped into `Very Short (<=5h)`, `Short (6h)`, `Recommended (7-8h)`, and `Long (9+h)`.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>combined_grip_kg</code></td>
<td><code>MGDCGSZ</code></td>
<td>Primary strength outcome (`kg`): sum of the largest dynamometer reading from the left hand and right hand across three alternating trials per hand (`MGDEXSTS == 1` complete bilateral test).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>max_hand_grip_kg</code></td>
<td><code>MGXH1T1–MGXH2T3</code></td>
<td>Secondary strength metric (`kg`): maximum single-hand isometric reading across all six recorded trials.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>race_ethnicity</code></td>
<td><code>RIDRETH3</code></td>
<td>Six-category NHANES race/Hispanic origin classification including Non-Hispanic Asian oversample (`2011–2014`).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>trouble_sleeping</code>, <code>sleep_disorder</code></td>
<td><code>SLQ050</code>, <code>SLQ060</code></td>
<td>Binary (`Yes` / `No`) indicators for ever telling a doctor about trouble sleeping (`SLQ050`) or being told by a doctor of a sleep disorder (`SLQ060`); codes `7`/`9` recoded to `NA`.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>income_pir</code></td>
<td><code>INDFMPIR</code></td>
<td>Ratio of family income to federal poverty threshold (`0.00` to `5.00`, top-coded at `5.00`).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>mec_weight_4yr</code>, <code>SDMVSTRA</code>, <code>SDMVPSU</code></td>
<td><code>DEMO_G/H</code></td>
<td>Four-year MEC examination weight (`WTMEC2YR / 2` per NCHS analytic guidelines for combining two 2-year waves), masked variance stratum (`29` non-overlapping strata), and nested primary sampling unit (`61` PSUs).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>

<!-- SURVEY DESIGN & UNWEIGHTED VS WEIGHTED EXPLANATION -->
<section class="glass-card">
<div class="section-kicker">Statistical Methodology</div>
<h2 class="section-title" style="margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Combined NHANES Complex Survey Design &amp; Estimation Modes</h2>
<div class="prose-block">
<p>
NHANES uses a stratified, multistage probability cluster design rather than simple random sampling. Following CDC/NCHS analytic guidelines for combining the 2011–2012 and 2013–2014 cycles, four-year Mobile Examination Center weights are constructed as <code>mec_weight_4yr = WTMEC2YR / 2</code>. Stratum identifiers (<code>SDMVSTRA</code>) are uniquely numbered across waves (`90–103` in 2011–2012; `104–118` in 2013–2014; zero overlap), with primary sampling units (<code>SDMVPSU</code>) nested within strata (`r n_strata` strata, `r n_psu` PSUs, `r n_degf` design degrees of freedom). To preserve full variance structure during subpopulation analysis, <code>survey::svydesign(..., nest = TRUE)</code> is initialized on all `r comma(n_mec_universe)` MEC-examined respondents (`WTMEC2YR > 0`) and restricted to the `r comma(n_total)`-examinee cohort via <code>subset()</code>.
</p>
<p>
<strong>Unweighted sample estimates vs. survey-weighted population estimates:</strong> Unweighted visualizations and sample statistics describe the exact `r comma(n_total)` individuals examined in NHANES—a cohort in which NCHS intentionally oversamples Non-Hispanic Black, Hispanic, Non-Hispanic Asian, low-income, and older participants to ensure reliable subgroup precision. Survey-weighted population estimates reweight observations by <code>mec_weight_4yr</code> to represent the civilian, non-institutionalized U.S. population aged `16+` and compute Taylor-series linearized standard errors and confidence intervals accounting for PSU clustering and stratification. Every visualization and regression table on this site explicitly labels which estimation mode is displayed.
</p>
</div>
</section>

<!-- REPRODUCIBILITY IN A FRESH CODESPACE -->
<section class="glass-card">
<div class="section-kicker">Computational Reproducibility</div>
<h2 class="section-title" style="margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Reproducing the Website in a Fresh Codespace</h2>
<div class="prose-block">
<p>
All R package dependencies (including <code>tidyverse</code>, <code>haven</code>, <code>survey</code>, <code>plotly</code>, <code>jsonlite</code>, <code>splines</code>, <code>broom</code>, <code>knitr</code>, and <code>scales</code>) are declared in the root <code>DESCRIPTION</code> file. From a fresh GitHub Codespace or local R/Quarto environment, run the following three commands at the terminal:
</p>
</div>

<div class="mini-panel" style="font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.86rem; color: #e2e8f0; line-height: 1.75; overflow-x: auto;">
# 1. Install all documented R dependencies (including survey >= 4.2)<br>
Rscript -e 'pak::local_install_deps()'<br><br>
# 2. (Optional) Re-generate data/processed/nhanes_sleep_strength.rds from raw CDC XPT files<br>
Rscript scripts/prepare_data.R<br><br>
# 3. Render all six pages of the Quarto website into _site/<br>
quarto render
</div>
